title: GitLab fixed a maximum-severity flaw on 12 October; a viral alert gives a different CVE number
dek: The audience is anyone running their own GitLab server. A widely shared alert names a CVE and a scope that do not match GitLab's own notice.
what: On Wednesday 21 October, The Hacker News posted an alert: a GitLab flaw rated CVSS 10.0 that it said affects 12 years of releases, numbered CVE-2026-110264, and that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed servers.

GitLab's own patch notice for release 19.4.2, dated 12 October 2026, lists a critical flaw numbered CVE-2026-97229, rated CVSS 10.0. It describes an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler. GitLab lists it as affecting 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2. The notice lists 24 fixes in all.

Two things in the post do not match that notice. The CVE number differs, and the critical flaw is listed only for three recent release lines, not twelve years of releases. The notice does list one medium-severity flaw, CVE-2026-101168, that affects versions from 12.0. I cannot say whether the post mixed these up or refers to something I did not find. The post links an article that I did not open.

The Hacker News's article on its own site, dated 13 October, uses the number CVE-2026-97229 and says the flaw could let unauthenticated users run code on the server. I found no report of attacks in the wild in the sources I read.
why: A CVSS 10.0 on software many companies host themselves is the kind of alert security accounts push hard, and a number in a short post is easy to get wrong.
next: Whether the post is corrected, and whether anyone reports exploitation of the flaw.

sources.label: The Hacker News: GitLab patches CVSS 10.0 flaw
